title: Central Banks Under Pressure
gist: Heading into the week of 15 September 2026, the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan both face the same triple bind: US political pressure, rising inflation and higher bond yields. Trump has threatened more protectionist trade policy if the Fed does not cut, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has sold euros to buy yen and claimed inside knowledge of BoJ intentions, raising Japanese fears that the BoJ looks subservient to Washington.

themes.theme: Fed and BoJ squeezed by the same three forces

insights.claim: The Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan are simultaneously facing political pressure, rising inflation and higher bond yields, making their September 2026 meetings the two that matter most in a week crowded with central bank decisions.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Two reaction functions are being tested at once; treat Fed and BoJ outcomes as a paired event risk for global duration and the dollar-yen cross rather than as separate local decisions.
insights.quote: Both face political pressure, rising inflation and higher bond yields, leaving investors keen to see how policymakers respond and how markets react.
insights.locator: Amid a slew of central bank meetings

insights.claim: With inflation rising and bond yields higher at the same time as politicians push for easier policy, the key uncertainty for investors is not the policy decision itself but how markets react to whether policymakers bend.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Watch the long end: a cut delivered into rising inflation is the setup where bond yields rise on easing rather than fall, steepening curves.
insights.locator: Amid a slew of central bank meetings

themes.theme: White House pressure on the Fed

insights.claim: Within the month to mid-September 2026, President Donald Trump threatened to impose more protectionist trade policies if the Federal Reserve does not cut interest rates, explicitly linking trade policy to monetary policy.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Tariff risk becomes a function of the Fed's decision, so a hold is a live catalyst for renewed trade escalation and for the inflation impulse that follows it.
insights.quote: President Donald Trump has threatened more protectionist trade policies if the Fed does not cut interest rates
insights.locator: The US administration has been pressuring both central banks

insights.claim: The US administration is applying pressure to foreign central banks as well as its own, extending the politicization of monetary policy beyond America's borders.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Central bank independence is becoming a cross-border risk premium, an argument for owning inflation hedges and steepeners over trusting stated reaction functions.
insights.quote: The US administration has been pressuring both central banks.
insights.locator: The US administration has been pressuring both central banks

themes.theme: Bessent's yen trade and BoJ credibility

insights.claim: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has personally sold euros to buy yen and has claimed to have inside information about the Bank of Japan's intentions, which is the basis of his bullish yen view.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A sitting Treasury Secretary positioned long yen against the euro is a policy signal as much as a trade; EUR/JPY carries a political tail risk that option pricing may not reflect.
insights.quote: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has sold euros to buy yen
insights.locator: Meanwhile, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent

insights.claim: Bessent's claim of inside knowledge has raised concerns in Japan that the Bank of Japan could appear subservient to the US government, putting the BoJ's perceived independence at stake alongside its rate decision.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The BoJ may need to act in a way that visibly contradicts Washington's stated expectations to defend its credibility, which cuts against consensus positioning on the yen and JGBs.
insights.quote: concerns in Japan that the BoJ could appear subservient to the US government.
insights.locator: This has raised concerns in Japan
